title: Live Visibility
eyebrow: Proposal · thread links that always show, and no long or quiet work without your OK

short.lead: You asked for three things now, not after the restructure (#306, reverted on 2026-10-28). First, every thread shows its own session link without being asked. Second, nothing runs quiet by default. Third, a long or quiet tool call needs your OK first; otherwise the work is split into short steps you can watch. The link goes missing because the plugin only builds it when CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECTS_SESSION is 1. This session is a cloud session started with CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 and a valid cse_ id, but CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECTS_SESSION is unset here, so no link was offered. Even inside a project thread, the link only appears in a checklist header.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what exists today and what this proposal adds.
items: Builds https://claude.ai/code/session_<id> from CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID. It is reused as it is; only the gate in front of it and where the link must appear change.
Blocks the end of a turn once when a Remote Control link or helper work trail was never posted. It gains one more case: the session's own link missing from the first reply.

Reads how long ago a helper's transcript or a command's output file was last written, and prints ok, STALLED or finished. Nothing calls it any more: #292 removed the 5-minute reminder on 2026-10-15. This proposal reuses it as the source of each progress line.

Dropped in #292 together with a guard that refused nohup, & and hidden windows. It comes back as a new rule in your words (see Changes). The old guard does not come back: the new check asks before long work instead of refusing background commands outright.

Since 2.48.0 a hook that looked and found nothing to do prints no line unless HOUSE_RULES_TRACE=verbose; the default is on, and off silences every line (house_rules/core.py, trace_enabled and trace_noop). Under your rule the default becomes verbose, and HOUSE_RULES_TRACE=on brings back today's quieter level.
A check before long or quiet calls

Before a tool call that will run long or show you nothing while it runs, the plugin stops it and has me ask you in a reply first, saying what it is and roughly how long. Without your OK I do the work in short steps instead.
Your OK when I ask, or nothing if short steps are fine.

I read it as a long helper agent or a long command, where today you see only the start and the end. If Trace is the name of a specific tool or step, tell me its name, because a hook can be pinned to it directly.
If my reading is wrong, put the name of the tool or step in your reply.

changes: chg
Changed gate: every cloud session with a session id gets its link (thread_link_note)
The link is offered whenever CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE is true and CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID has the cse_ shape, not only in project threads.
A cloud session started from a project thread, like this one, gets no link and is hard to find again.
Its first reply opens with "Transcript of this session" as a link, with the raw id beside it.
Checked on this session's own variables: CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true, a cse_ id, CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECTS_SESSION unset. Links still never reach git, because the credit guard from #405 is unchanged.
chg
Changed rule text: the link opens the first reply, plus the checklist header in a project thread
The injected instruction asks for the link at the top of the first reply, and the links-owed check blocks once if it is missing.
The link appears only if a checklist is posted.
The link is the first thing you see in every thread.
In a plain cloud session there is no post_message tool, so the check reads the first reply's text instead.
chg
New rule text: nothing is quiet by default, and long work is asked for first

One section in house-rules.md, in your words: work, thoughts and processes are never hidden in a way you can't easily find; anything quieted names the switch that shows it; a long or quiet tool call is asked for first, and otherwise the work goes in short visible steps.
Since #292 there is no rule about this at all.
Every session reads your standard at start.
Replaces nothing that exists today; the old rule's file stays in _to_delete/.
chg
New check: long or quiet calls are stopped until you OK them (PreToolUse)

Stops a call that will run over 1 minute or show nothing while it runs: a command with a timeout over 60 seconds, sleep or wait loops, run_in_background, Monitor, and a foreground helper agent (see the helpers choice). The refusal tells me to ask you or split the work.
I can start a call that runs for many minutes and shows you nothing.
I ask first, or you see a run of short steps.
Your OK in a message lets through the one call I asked about, not every later one. HOUSE_RULES_LONG_CALLS=off turns the check off.
chg
Changed default: hook trace lines print unless turned down
HOUSE_RULES_TRACE defaults to verbose instead of on; setting it to on brings back today's behaviour, and off still silences every line.
A hook that found nothing to do prints nothing.
Every hook says it ran and what it decided.

Cost: one more line on your screen per hook call. The lines are sent as systemMessage, which the app shows you; I have not measured whether they also take up room in my context, and the build measures it with tools/measure_footprint.py.
chg
New hook: progress lines for long work you have approved

While long work you approved runs, the thread posts a line at least every 2 minutes: what it is doing, how long it has run, and when the work last wrote anything (from stallcheck.py, which gains an --every flag). A stuck run says STALLED in words.
An approved long run would still look stuck.
You can tell running from stuck at any moment.
UNTESTED: I have not yet confirmed that a watch line wakes a project thread mid-task; the build proves it on a real thread before anything relies on it.
choices: sessions
Which sessions show their own link?
A
Every cloud session with a session id, including sessions a project thread starts
Covers the case you hit: this session had no link.
B
Project threads only, as today
Smallest change, but cloud sessions stay linkless.
Option A fixes the session you are reading now.
where
Where does the link appear?
A
First line of the first reply, plus the checklist header in a project thread, enforced by the end-of-turn check
You see it without opening anything.
B
Checklist header only, as today
Threads without a checklist never show it.
Option A makes it show by default, which is what you asked for.
ask
How do I ask before a long or quiet call?
A
The check stops the call and I ask in my reply; your next message saying yes lets that one call through
Works in project threads, where an app permission prompt may never reach you.
B
The app's own permission prompt pops up for each one
One tap, but it may not show in a project thread or on your phone.
Option A, because it works on every surface you use.
helpers
Do helper agents count as long calls?
A
Yes: I ask before each helper, and the delegation rule says so
Matches what you said; today's delegation rule sends most building to helpers, so you will see more of those questions.
B
No: helpers run without asking, but must post progress lines
Fewer questions, but a helper is still a long call you didn't OK.
Option A. This changes the "Once the approach is decided, delegate the execution" rule, so it needs your pick.

wrapup.summary: Every session opens with its own link, nothing runs quiet by default, and any long or quiet call waits for your OK; without it, the work comes in short steps you can watch.
wrapup.changing: One gate and one instruction in house_rules/delegation.py, a new check before long calls, the trace default flipped, a progress hook with a new stallcheck.py flag, one rule section, plus tests, docs and a version bump. It builds on today's 2.74.1 code, not the reverted restructure.
wrapup.blocking: Your answers to the four choices above, and whether my reading of "running a Trace" is right.
wrapup.next: I file the build issues, build on AjsAgent/thread-links-trace-visibility-4eoxf3, prove the progress line on a real project thread, and hand it over with a QA page.
